abstract: Abstract Magnetic memory technology continues to drive progress in non-volatile data storage, offering significant advantages in data retention and operational endurance. As a key component in memory architectures, the magnetic tunnel junction (MTJ) plays a central role in the development of modern spintronics by leveraging its bistable resistance states. The emergence of two-dimensional (2D) magnetic materials has further accelerated the advancement of high-performance MTJs, capitalizing on their exceptional magnetic properties and ideal van der Waals interfaces. This review begins by introducing 2D magnetic materials with diverse properties, encompassing both layered and non-layered structures. It then summarizes novel magnetic tunnel junctions engineered from these 2D materials. Next, the review outlines recent applications and progress in theoretical calculations pertinent to 2D magnetic tunnel junctions. Finally, it discusses future opportunities for employing 2D magnetic materials in the design of innovative MTJs for next-generation high-performance electronics.

title: Asymptotical event-based boundary fault-tolerant control for cascaded ODE-belt systems with prescribed-time performance
abstract: Abstract This paper focuses on event-based boundary fault-tolerant control for deferred-constrained cascaded ordinary differential equation (ODE)-belt systems modeled by flexible axially moving belt and nonlinear actuator dynamics subject to unknown parameters, nonlinearities, and actuator failure. To reduce the continuous updating of input signal, a dynamic threshold triggering mechanism is developed. Under these multiple constraints, achieving the asymptotic convergence of cascaded systems presents significant challenges for control design. In control design, radial basis neural networks are used to approximate uncertain nonlinear functions. The prescribed performance funnel and adaptive backstepping technique are applied to skillfully achieve the prescribed performance. Based on the designed adaptive failure compensator, the effect of actuator fault can be compensated for completely. Based on the Barrier Lyapunov function (BLF) approach, a novel boundary event-based fault-tolerant control protocol is successfully designed to achieve asymptotic convergence and vibration suppression. Remarkably, the appealing feature of the designed controller lies in the smooth function norm with a positive integrable function, which makes the controller powerful enough to achieve asymptotic convergence. Furthermore, the Zeno behavior can be excluded. Lastly, some simulation results are presented to validate the constructed results.

title: Consensus-optimized decentralized fine-tuning of foundation models for 6G agentic AI networks
Symbiotic radios for future ambient IoT
abstract: Abstract In recent years, there has been an extensive deployment of the Internet of Things (IoT) across various vertical industries. However, this progress comes with the challenges of accommodating billions of IoT devices, leading to significant issues in power consumption, spectrum allocation, and device costs. Ambient IoT, empowered by energy harvesting and low-power communication techniques such as backscatter communications, stands out as a promising technology supporting massive net-zero connections. Notably, both 3GPP and IEEE 802.11 have initiated standardization research in this area, through which ambient IoT devices have been well identified with their advantages in terms of low power consumption and low cost. Despite these benefits, ambient IoT still faces challenges in integrating with existing legitimate communication networks, particularly regarding the spectrum issue and the ambient signal utilization issue. Fortunately, symbiotic radio (SR) offers a promising solution by introducing cooperation between the legitimate transmission and the IoT transmission. In this article, we provide a comprehensive tutorial on SR-enabled future ambient IoT. Specifically, we first present the fundamentals of ambient IoT and then introduce SR within this context, as well as highlighting its advantages in ambient IoT. Following that, we focus on addressing three important issues for SR in ambient IoT: cooperative modulation design, multiple access design, and resource allocation from the perspective of communication design. Moreover, we highlight future research directions in this emerging field.

title: Transcending natural evolution in the age of artificial intelligence
abstract: Abstract Artificial intelligence (AI) is undergoing a fundamental transition from digital representational models to embodied, physically situated systems. This position paper characterises this shift as the crossing of an embodiment threshold, where Al’s operational capacity becomes integrated with physical environments and neural substrates. We argue that this transition is defined by a profound evolutionary tempo mismatch between rapid algorithmic iteration and the millennial-scale inertia of biological evolution. By synthesising advances in flexible bioelectronics and high-bandwidth neural decoding, we examine the biophysical mechanisms that could enable human-machine symbiosis while exposing the thermodynamic and material constraints that accompany this trajectory. In particular, we contrast the brain’s highly efficient metabolic architecture with the resource-intensive scaling of silicon-based computation, highlighting the risk that the infrastructure required for large-scale augmentation may produce durable socio-technical stratification. We therefore contend that the central challenge of this era lies in governing neuro-computational co-evolution rather than merely regulating standalone AI systems. In this context, governance is not merely a regulatory constraint, but a deliberative mechanism for shaping whether, how, and under what conditions deeper human-machine integration should proceed. To address this shift, we propose an adaptive governance framework centred on infrastructural legibility, operational safety, and neural privacy. This roadmap outlines a strategic architecture for navigating the transition towards secure and equitable forms of human-machine symbiosis.

title: A radius-constrained interval estimation method for unobservable systems
E3-Agent: an executable and evolving agent for resource management of edge generative inference
abstract: Edge deployments of generative inference increasingly face two practical realities: per-device per-model performance is often unknown at deployment time, and it is non-stationary due to user-driven semantic events, background load, and device churn. Consequently, a resource manager that is tuned offline under a fixed regime can become brittle and expensive to maintain. This paper presents $E^3$-Agent, an executable and evolving agent for edge artificial intelligence generated content (AIGC) resource management. $E^3$-Agent separates a fast-path router that makes millisecond-level dispatch decisions from a slow-path, event-driven large language model (LLM) meta-controller that mitigates regime shifts through a small, explicit control surface exposed via a tool interface, including risk gating, router configuration, and rapid performance calibration. The agent learns online from execution feedback and continuously adapts to unknown and time-varying service-time mappings. We evaluate $E^3$-Agent in a discrete-event simulator driven by MLPerf-derived device-model measurement priors, covering cold-start warmup and three dynamic regimes: semantic dynamics, device churn, and hidden drift. Across the dynamic scenarios, $E^3$-Agent reduces average latency by 65%-73% compared to the best static baseline, stays within 7%-10% of an online full-information Oracle used for evaluation, and effectively suppresses stutter rate under semantic degradation.

title: Governing the commons via adaptive incentive control with real-time feedback
Practical phase-coding side-channel-secure quantum key distribution
abstract: All kinds of device loopholes give rise to a great obstacle to practical secure quantum key distribution (QKD). In this article, inspired by the original side-channel-secure protocol [Physical Review Applied 12, 054034 (2019)], a new QKD protocol called phase-coding side-channel-secure (PC-SCS) protocol is proposed. This protocol can be immune to all uncorrelated side channels of the source part and all loopholes of the measurement side. A finite-key security analysis against coherent attack of the new protocol is given. The proposed protocol only requires modulation of two phases, which can avoid the challenge of preparing perfect vacuum states. Numerical simulation shows that a practical transmission distance of 300 km can be realized by the PC-SCS protocol.

title: Cross-reality location privacy protection in 6G-enabled vehicular metaverses: an LLM-enhanced hybrid generative diffusion model-based approach
abstract: The emergence of 6G-enabled vehicular metaverses enables Autonomous Vehicles (AVs) to operate across physical and virtual spaces through space-air-ground-sea integrated networks. The AVs can deploy AI agents powered by large AI models as personalized assistants, on edge servers to support intelligent driving decision making and enhanced on-board experiences. However, such cross-reality interactions may cause serious location privacy risks, as adversaries can infer AV trajectories by correlating the location reported when AVs request LBS in reality with the location of the edge servers on which their corresponding AI agents are deployed in virtuality. To address this challenge, we design a cross-reality location privacy protection framework based on hybrid actions, including continuous location perturbation in reality and discrete privacy-aware AI agent migration in virtuality. In this framework, a new privacy metric, termed cross-reality location entropy, is proposed to effectively quantify the privacy levels of AVs. Based on this metric, we formulate an optimization problem to optimize the hybrid action, focusing on achieving a balance between location protection, service latency reduction, and quality of service maintenance. To solve the complex mixed-integer problem, we develop a novel LLM-enhanced Hybrid Diffusion Proximal Policy Optimization (LHDPPO) algorithm, which integrates LLM-driven informative reward design to enhance environment understanding with double Generative Diffusion Models-based policy exploration to handle high-dimensional action spaces, thereby enabling reliable determination of optimal hybrid actions. Extensive experiments on real-world datasets demonstrate that the proposed framework effectively mitigates cross-reality location privacy leakage for AVs while maintaining strong user immersion within 6G-enabled vehicular metaverse scenarios.

title: A fine-grained diffusion prototype for real-time intrusion detection
Erratum to: LLM-enhanced-EA-driven automated optimization framework for joint indoor deployment of multiple BSs and RISs
Virtual-CNTM: a digital twin model for cultured neural tissue on microelectrode array based on spike neuromorphic network
From general-purpose LLM to specialized beamforming for low-altitude ISAC networks: a LoRA-based multi-expert framework
abstract: Integrated sensing and communications (ISAC) jointly ensure both sensing and transmission performance, where beamforming design serves as the key to unlocking its potential and typically involves coupled constraints and complex mathematical optimization. Recently, large language models (LLMs) leverage their extensive prior knowledge to demonstrate remarkable potential in mathematical reasoning. Integrating LLMs into ISAC optimization has thus attracted considerable attention as a promising direction. However, most existing studies simply treat the LLM as a numerical encoder trained in a regression framework, which fails to adapt a generalpurpose model into a task-oriented expert. In this paper, we pioneer the use of LLMs to construct an end-to-end ISAC optimizer and design a multi-expert framework that enables adaptation to diverse ISAC scenarios. Leveraging the strength of LLMs in natural language (NL) understanding, we reformulate the task scenario into NL descriptions, which not only capture the semantic relationships between the optimization objective and the constraints to facilitate model reasoning, but also eliminate the reliance on manual data preprocessing. Furthermore, inspired by the mixture-of-experts paradigm, we build upon a shared LLM backbone and endow it with specialized ISAC knowledge for diverse requirements through low-rank adaptation. We develop a two-stage training framework. In the supervised fine-tuning stage, the model learns the supervised mapping from scenario descriptions to structured beamforming solutions, while reinforcement learning (RL) further optimizes constraint satisfaction and objective quality. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our approach achieves superior performance, significantly outperforming existing AI-based methods. Our code is available at https://github.com/BUAA-SIC-LAB/LLM4BF .

title: Realizing 88-Gbps 2×2 MIMO transmission at D-band over a 30-km wireless link enabled by I/Q MRC-based SNR-enhancement technology
High-performance computing in transition: from peak performance to HPC-enabled scientific exploration
Agentic AI-aided resource allocation for multi-task and multi-modal semantic communications
abstract: Semantic communication (SemCom) enables task-oriented transmission by directly conveying semantic information, but in multi-modal and multi-task scenarios, dynamic traffic arrivals and channel variations intensify the coupling among semantic quality, quality of service (QoS) constraints, and resource consumption, making fixed slicing structures or single control policies ineffective. Meanwhile, Agentic AI—empowered by large foundation models—has recently attracted growing attention for enabling intent-driven, closed-loop decision-making in complex network control and orchestration. To address this challenge, we propose an Agentic AI-driven multi-modal and multi-task SemCom framework (AAMTSC), which jointly optimizes network slicing and continuous resource allocation through a hierarchical closed-loop design. The main contributions of this work are threefold. First, we develop an Agentic AI architecture for SemCom network slicing and decompose the coupled joint optimization into two coordinated decision layers: structural orchestration and online control. Second, we propose an intelligent network slice orchestrator (INSO)-Agent for slice structuring and key parameter configuration, generating interpretable structural priors and preference constraints to guide resource scheduling. Third, we propose a network slice resource optimizer (NSRO)-Agent for continuous online resource optimization and tightly couple it with the structural layer via feedback coordination, thereby improving adaptability to dynamic traffic loads and time-varying channels. Simulation results show that AAMTSC consistently outperforms strong baselines under varying arrival rates and signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) conditions, achieving up to 38.6% improvement in long-term system utility \({\overline J}\) and 36.8% gain in constraint satisfaction ( S a ), demonstrating its effectiveness and robustness in dynamic SemCom environments.

title: Role of thick AlN insertion layer in modulating the electronic and thermal characteristics of AlGaN/GaN/AlN/Graded-AlGaN/GaN double-channel HEMTs
Single-photodiode 600-Gb/s scale-across optical interconnect with simplified O/E frontend correction
Event-triggered visual neuron based on memristor for privacy-preserving and efficient neuromorphic sensing
abstract: Biological visual neurons encode changes in light intensity through joint modulation of spike polarity and frequency, enabling efficient detection of dynamic events and significantly reducing sensory data redundancy. However, existing neuromorphic sensors with the biomimetic neuron spiking characteristics are still lacking. Here, we propose an event-triggered visual neuron that combines light sensing and frequency-based encoding in a compact structure. This architecture maps biological neuron behavior onto hardware, producing bipolar spike trains with frequencies ranging from 58.3 to 191.4 kHz that reflect luminance variation, with a dynamic range over 100 dB. Unlike conventional sensors, the event-triggered visual neuron circuit directly encodes changes into frequency-modulated pulses, mimicking retinal dynamics and suppressing static leakage. Experiments show event-triggered visual neuron outputs resist deep learning-based privacy attacks: recognition accuracy on event data drops to chance levels, while remaining high on original videos. We further developed a neuromorphic pose estimation framework based on event-triggered visual neuron output, achieving keypoint recognition accuracy comparable to conventional frame-based methods while significantly reducing power consumption and data bandwidth requirements.

title: Superadditive cross-modal transistor neuron for a hybrid in-sensor computing system
abstract: Inspired by the cross-modal perception and processing mechanisms dominated by the biological visual system, we present an ion-exciton dual-induced superadditive cross-modal transistor neuron (SCTN) for the first time. Owing to a synergistic mechanism of electric-double-layer-driven π -electron delocalization and exciton dissociation jointly, the device realizes outstanding weight regulation capabilities and superadditive response characteristics. Under cross-modal stimulation, it demonstrates the highest weight-update efficiency and relaxation controllability for incoming sequential signals, achieving optimal performance in both Morse code decoding and in-sensor computing tasks, significantly outperforming unimodal stimulation. Furthermore, by exploiting its nonlinear storage states, we also first construct a cross-modal reservoir computing system based on SCTN, and achieve high-accuracy recognition for both letter images and Morse code with minimal training, showcasing its potential for edge-oriented neuromorphic applications. This work not only introduces a novel device concept but also provides a new approach and hardware foundation for the development of efficient and compact neuromorphic systems tailored to edge intelligence scenarios.

title: 100 Gb/s integrated secure communication at D-band enabled by dual-stage chaotic model over 26 km
Diffusion model-based radio map reconstruction for low-altitude wireless networks
abstract: Radio maps describe the spatial distribution of wireless channel quality and support spectrum management for low-altitude operations. Recent diffusion-based methods have advanced radio map reconstruction under limited measurements, but existing pipelines design data acquisition to improve reconstruction and assume that measurements are available to the ground server without transmission rate constraints. In practice, the transmission rate constraint limits the number of measurements that reach the ground server within the mission time budget and can impose severe uplink delay. This delay renders the measurements temporally inconsistent with the time-varying radio environment, thereby degrading the accuracy of radio map reconstruction. This paper proposes a communication-aware framework for UAV-assisted dynamic radio map reconstruction under a closed-loop sensing and uploading workflow. The framework consists of a communication-aware active sampling block and a generation block. The communication-aware active sampling block formulates sensing as a Markov decision process, learns a route-constrained sampling policy that accounts for uplink delay, and aligns sparse, asynchronous measurements to a target time via a spatio-temporal Gaussian process. The generation block uses a conditional diffusion model to synthesize high-fidelity radio maps at target time instants from the aligned sparse observations. Extensive simulations across different mission time budgets and bandwidths show that the proposed method yields reductions in covariance trace and root mean square error (RMSE) at the end of the mission of up to 6.4% and 7.3% over the communication-unaware baseline, and up to 44.2% and 42.5% over open-loop baselines.

title: A heterogeneous CIM/CNM architecture for LMs utilizing speed/density-optimized 3D CAA-IGZO DRAMs
abstract: Large artificial intelligence models (LMs) based on the Transformer have demonstrated superior performance in many applications. The encoder (prefill) and decoder parts of LMs show significant differences in the compute-to-memory ratio and the memory speed/density requirement. Recently, the emerging Indium-Gallium-Zinc-Oxide (IGZO) transistor has become a promising memory candidate for LM architectures, featuring ultra-low leakage current and high-density monolithic 3D fabrication. Unfortunately, prior studies primarily emphasize device-level fabrication, while overlooking critical circuit-level requirements for practical applications and the parasitic effects inherent in practical manufacturing. This paper proposes 3DIG-CXM, the first 3D-IGZO-based computing-in/near-memory (CIM/CNM) architecture for LMs. The highlights include (1) for compute-bound LM encoder, we propose a speed-optimized 3D-3T0C IGZO DRAM array that supports 2D full-layer-copy fast read ability to satisfy the high-performance CIM engines, enabling 3.45× higher read frequency; (2) for memory-bound LM decoder, we propose a density-optimized 3D-2T0C IGZO DRAM array featuring underneath peripheral and CNM circuits for ultra-high storage density; (3) a 3D parasitic effect evaluation method is built to explore the maximum 3D dimensions; (4) a pipelined workflow based on the speed/density-optimized IGZO arrays is proposed for the heterogeneous CIM/CNM architecture. Experiment results illustrate that the 3DIG-CXM achieves 25.9× area savings compared with the SRAM CIM baseline, and 1.2×∓3.0× energy efficiency on the encoder/decoder compared to the off-chip HBM baseline.

title: TokenCom: vision-language model for multimodal and multitask token communications
abstract: Visual-Language Models (VLMs), with their strong capabilities in image and text understanding, offer a solid foundation for intelligent communications. However, their effectiveness is constrained by limited token granularity, overlong visual token sequences, and inadequate cross-modal alignment. To overcome these challenges, we propose TaiChi, a novel VLM framework designed for token communications. TaiChi adopts a dual-visual tokenizer architecture that processes both high- and low-resolution images to collaboratively capture pixel-level details and global conceptual features. A Bilateral Attention Network (BAN) is introduced to intelligently fuse multi-scale visual tokens, thereby enhancing visual understanding and producing compact visual tokens. In addition, a Kolmogorov Arnold Network (KAN)-based modality projector with learnable activation functions is employed to achieve precise nonlinear alignment from visual features to the text semantic space, thus minimizing information loss. Finally, TaiChi is integrated into a multimodal and multitask token communication system equipped with a joint VLM-channel coding scheme. Experimental results validate the superior performance of TaiChi, as well as the feasibility and effectiveness of the TaiChi-driven token communication system.

title: A token/KV-cache communication media selection and resource allocation strategy for multi-agent collaboration
abstract: The convergence of large language models (LLMs) with 6G networks is fostering a paradigm of autonomous multi-agent cooperation, which in turn is expected to substantially increase east-west traffic. Although latent-space interaction mechanisms can enable more efficient collaboration than symbolic natural-language (NL) exchanges, prior work often abstracts away the associated communication overhead under practical wireless constraints. In embodied multi-agent settings, heterogeneous interaction media incur disparate inference and transmission costs, thereby inducing an inherent end-to-end (E2E) latency trade-off. To address this, we propose a joint design that integrates communication-media selection with wireless resource allocation. Through analytical characterization and simulation-based evaluation, we show that neither token-based transmission nor key-value (KV) cache-based transmission is uniformly optimal across operating regimes, as performance depends critically on system parameters such as available computational resources and channel conditions. Accordingly, we formulate a joint optimization problem aimed at minimizing the E2E latency of multi-agent collaboration and develop a low-complexity joint media selection and resource allocation (JMSRA) algorithm. Numerical results further confirm that, by adaptively coordinating the interaction media and bandwidth allocation over heterogeneous links, the proposed scheme achieves markedly reduced E2E latency relative to conventional NL-only and KV-cache-only baselines, enabling efficient and robust multi-agent collaboration in future wireless networks.

title: High-linearity AlN/GaN HEMT with OIP3/PDC of 10.5 dB at 30 GHz using transitional 2DEG density control technology
Optimized contact plan design for reflector and phased array terminals in cislunar space networks
Lunar-based bistatic SAR: Earth observation capability and spatiotemporal variations
Agent-defined architecture: make 6G a conversational and thinking network
abstract: The rapid development of large language models (LLMs) and artificial intelligence (AI) agent technologies has motivated the mobile industry to rethink AI-oriented services and AI-native networks. This shift provides opportunities to fundamentally evolve the next generation of mobile networks from being connection-centric to becoming intent-based, task-oriented, and autonomously adaptive. This paper proposes a novel agent-defined architecture (ADA) to make the sixth-generation (6G) network a conversational and thinking network. This new design paradigm first paves the way for users and applications to interact with the network through intents for both network demands and application services. A System Agent is introduced to enable the network to “think”, thereby natively supporting intent parsing, task decomposition, and coordination among domain-specific agents. These capabilities are achieved through a three-layer architectural design comprising the intent handling, network agent, and network tool layers, with the design motivations, principles, key features, and challenges presented. An extended reality (XR) use case is illustrated to show the end-to-end architectural workflow. Prototype-based evaluations and resource utilization analysis further show that ADA supports intent-driven orchestration, reduces signaling latency, and keeps the additional resource overhead manageable under concurrent intent-processing loads.

title: Picosecond-scale time transfer over a 5756 km field fiber-optic link via real-time dispersion self-calibration
Sequence-ratio optical coding for joint localization and communication in four-beacon underwater systems
A THz omnidirectional AiP system based on hybrid wafer-level packaged process for chip-to-chip wireless interconnect applications
On nonlinear dimensionality reduction, linear smoothing, and boundary conditions
abstract: Abstract We develop theory for nonlinear dimensionality reduction (NLDR). While a large number of NLDR methods have been proposed in the literature, there is limited understanding of how these methods work and how they interrelate. Also, existing theory provides little in the way of leverage for devising new algorithms. We provide a novel theoretical framework for the analysis of NLDR based on a connection to the statistical theory of linear smoothers. This allows us to both understand existing methods and derive new ones. We use this connection to show that existing NLDR methods correspond asymptotically to discrete approximations of the solutions of sets of differential equations given a boundary condition. In particular, we can characterize many existing methods in terms of just three limiting differential operators and boundary conditions. Our theory also provides a way to assert that one method is preferable to another; indeed, we show that local tangent space alignment is superior within a class of methods that assume that a global coordinate chart defines an isometric embedding of the manifold.

title: AI4Research: a survey of artificial intelligence for scientific research
abstract: Abstract Recent advancements in artificial intelligence (AI), particularly in large language models (LLMs) such as OpenAI-o1 and DeepSeek-R1, have demonstrated remarkable capabilities in complex domains such as logical reasoning and experimental coding. Motivated by these advancements, numerous studies have explored the application of AI in the innovation process, particularly in the context of scientific research. These AI technologies primarily aim to develop systems that can autonomously conduct research processes across a wide range of scientific disciplines. Despite these significant strides, a comprehensive survey on AI for research (AI4Research) remains absent, which hampers our understanding and impedes further development in this field. To address this gap, we present a comprehensive survey and offer a unified perspective on AI4Research. Specifically, the main contributions of our work are as follows. (1) Systematic taxonomy: We first introduce a systematic taxonomy to classify five mainstream tasks in AI4Research. (2) New frontiers: Then, we identify key research gaps and highlight promising future directions, focusing on the rigor and scalability of automated experiments, as well as the societal impact. (3) Abundant applications and resources: Finally, we compile a wealth of resources, including relevant multidisciplinary applications, data corpora, and tools. We hope our work will provide the research community with quick access to these resources and stimulate innovative breakthroughs in AI4Research. All data and resources are publicly available at https://github.com/LightChen233/Awesome-AI4Research .

title: State estimation with protecting exogenous inputs via Cramér-Rao lower bound approach
abstract: Abstract This paper addresses the real-time state estimation problem for dynamic systems while protecting exogenous inputs against adversaries, who may be honest-but-curious third parties or external eavesdroppers. The Cramér-Rao lower bound (CRLB) is employed to constrain the mean square error (MSE) of the adversary’s estimate for the exogenous inputs above a specified threshold. By minimizing the MSE of the state estimate while ensuring a certain privacy level measured by CRLB, the problem is formulated as a constrained optimization. To solve the optimization problem, an explicit expression for CRLB is first provided. As the computational complexity of the CRLB increases with the time step, a low-complexity approach is proposed to make the complexity independent of time. Then, a relaxation approach is proposed to efficiently solve the optimization problem. Finally, a privacy-preserving state estimation algorithm with low complexity is developed, which also ensures ( ϵ, δ )-differential privacy. Two illustrative examples, including a practical scenario for protecting building occupancy, demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.

title: Towards semantic-based agent communication networks: vision, technologies, and challenges
abstract: Abstract The International Telecommunication Union (ITU) identifies “artificial intelligence (AI) and communication” as one of six key usage scenarios for 6G. Agentic AI, characterized by its capabilities in multi-modal environmental sensing, complex task coordination, and continuous self-optimization, is anticipated to drive the evolution toward agent-based communication networks. Semantic communication (SemCom), in turn, has emerged as a transformative paradigm that offers task-oriented efficiency, enhanced reliability in complex environments, and dynamic adaptation in resource allocation. However, comprehensive reviews that trace their technological evolution in the contexts of agent communications remain scarce. Addressing this gap, this paper systematically explores the role of semantics in agent communication networks. We first propose a novel architecture for semantic-based agent communication networks, structured into three layers, four entities, and four stages. Three wireless agent network layers define the logical structure and organization of entity interactions: the intention extraction and understanding layer, the semantic encoding and processing layer, and the distributed autonomy and collaboration layer. Across these layers, four AI agent entities, namely embodied agents, communication agents, network agents, and application agents, coexist and perform distinct tasks. Furthermore, four operational stages of semantic-enhanced agentic AI systems, namely perception, memory, reasoning, and action, form a cognitive cycle guiding agent behavior. Based on the proposed architecture, we provide a comprehensive review of the state-of-the-art on how semantics enhance agent communication networks. Finally, we identify key challenges and present potential solutions to offer directional guidance for future research in this emerging field.

title: Evolving embodied intelligence via reinforcement learning: challenges, barriers, and pathways
abstract: Abstract Embodied artificial intelligence—which involves agents perceiving, reasoning, and acting within physical environments—represents a new frontier towards artificial general intelligence. This study explores the evolving landscape of embodied intelligence, and presents a comprehensive survey on leveraging reinforcement learning (RL) to enhance embodied intelligence, systematically addressing the evolution from single-task performance in controlled settings to sophisticated cross-environment and cross-task capabilities. The study delves into several virtuoso capabilities, such as morphological intelligence (MI), human-like values and ethics, spontaneous reward generation, and reflective equilibrium. These capabilities are essential for developing adaptable, ethical, and intelligent embodied agents capable of navigating complex real-world scenarios. Furthermore, the study identifies and analyzes critical barriers in embodied RL, including sample efficiency, generalization and transferability, safety and robustness, real-time learning and adaptation, and interpretability and transparency. For each of these barriers, we offer an overview of current approaches and propose potential avenues for future research.

title: All-SiC integrated process platform: development roadmap and challenges
abstract: Abstract With exceptional high-temperature tolerance and radiation hardness, Silicon carbide (SiC) integrated circuits (ICs) have emerged as a promising candidate for extreme-environment applications in automotive, aerospace and deep-well drilling. This paper provides a comprehensive review of monolithic SiC IC platforms, encompassing a low-voltage (LV) IC platform incorporating exclusively LV devices and a power IC platform featuring concurrent integration of high-voltage (HV) and LV devices. Fundamental components evolve from bipolar junction transistors (BJTs) to junction field-effect transistors (JFETs), and subsequently to metal-oxide-semiconductor field-effect transistors (MOSFETs). A systematic review is conducted on the state-of-the-art and key technical hurdles for each device platform, with a focus on high-temperature and radiation-hardened applications. Finally, critical challenges confronting MOSFET-based integration process platforms are delineated, namely threshold voltage ( V th ) mismatch between NMOS and PMOS devices and radiation reliability issues, necessitating focused research initiatives to propel the industrialization of SiC monolithic ICs.

title: An ultra-wideband 50-to-110 GHz down-converter integrated with amplifier multiplier chains in 100 nm GaAs for 6G applications
Two-stage instance selection domain adaptation for diagnostic classification of neuropsychiatric disorders
abstract: Neuropsychiatric disorders are particularly serious health issues that affect the cognitive ability, emotion and behavior of individuals. The increasing prevalence and severe symptoms reflect the urgent need for effective diagnostic classification methods for neuropsychiatric disorders. Recent studies combine multi-site functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) data and domain adaptation techniques to address this problem. However, most related studies primarily focus on feature matching across the source and target domains, neglecting the issue of negative transfer brought by source data that exhibit low relevance with the target domain. In this study, we propose a two-stage instance selection domain adaptation algorithm (TS-ISDA) to tackle this issue. Specifically, we propose the minimum transfer distance (MTD) for direct distance measurement between a given sample and distribution. The MTD-based source instance selection and the target instance refinement steps are performed progressively to filter out unrelated source data and target instances with low-quality pseudo labels to ensure the effectiveness of the category-level feature alignment process. Then the local maximum mean discrepancy between the selected source and target data is calculated as the domain alignment loss. We conduct cross-site diagnostic classification studies of schizophrenia (SCZ), major depressive disorder (MDD) and autism spectrum disorder (ASD) based on fMRI data of 1003, 1043 and 607 participants from six sites, respectively. TS-ISDA achieves the highest average accuracies of 81.2%, 68.2% and 69.3% for SCZ, MDD and ASD, respectively, outperforming state-of-the-art methods. Furthermore, the discriminative brain regions identified by TS-ISDA show that the orbitofrontal cortex and the middle temporal gyrus regions consistently contribute significantly to the diagnosis of SCZ, MDD and ASD, guiding the search for biomarkers of various neuropsychiatric disorders.

title: A multimodal learning framework for protein function prediction based on multi-grained joint embedding
Asynchronous amplitude histogram-based multi-parameter monitoring for M-PAM optical communication channels
3.23 GW/cm2 power figure of merit and 0.69 V turn-on voltage β-Ga2O3 heterojunction barrier Schottky diodes with p-i-n junction termination
A versatile digital twin framework for maritime communications with off-the-shelf components
Can a CNN perform well on network traffic matrices? A case study on formulating network data to maximize the benefits of deep learning
abstract: With deep learning (DL) revolutionizing networking research, it has become trendy to cast network problems (e.g., networking prediction and control) as machine-learning tasks. The prevailing belief holds that by inputting all relevant information into a DL model and training it with a fitting loss function, DL’s remarkable capability will uncover an optimal solution. However, this optimistic view often does not hold true. This work presents a case study highlighting the necessity and challenges of carefully formulating network data to enable DL models to effectively understand network problems and capture domain-specific structures within a network. Traffic matrices (TMs), which detail the traffic volume for source-destination pairs and their temporal patterns, are crucial for network management tasks like traffic engineering and resource provisioning. Given their matrix structure and inherent spatial patterns, TMs might superficially resemble images, suggesting computer vision techniques like convolutional neural networks (CNNs) could be suitable for TM modeling and prediction. Yet, our attempts to train CNNs for TM interpolation were unsuccessful. We noted that CNNs excel at extracting features from data with spatial locality, which TMs lack due to the non-adjacent nature of correlated traffic patterns. To address this issue, we introduce a novel module that reorganizes TMs through weighted permutation matrices, thus enhancing the representation of traffic structure in a form more amenable to CNN processing. Our extensive testing confirms the effectiveness of our method in a range of TM-related tasks, including temporal interpolation, prediction, and completion.

title: RAGMIT: rapid APT group malware identification technology
Autonomous machine learning
Spatial-temporal knowledge fusion for continual learning in spiking neural networks
State space models meet remote sensing: a survey
abstract: Abstract State space models (SSMs), designed for long-range modeling, offer linear computational complexity and strong capabilities in capturing long-range dependencies. In the field of remote sensing, SSMs have gained popularity due to their effectiveness in addressing unique challenges such as dense visual predictions, multi-modal remote sensing data, and temporal remote sensing data, which have also yielded significant advancements in customized architectures. This study presents a comprehensive review of SSM-based approaches in remote sensing, covering most of the relevant studies since SSMs were first introduced to the field. We offer a multi-dimensional analysis examining SSM applications in remote sensing tasks and discussing advancements in architecture design. This study not only synthesizes the rapid progress in SSM-based research but also identifies key challenges and future opportunities. By providing a detailed perspective, this study aims to serve as a foundational resource for remote sensing researchers, offering actionable insights to foster further advancements in this evolving domain. We will keep tracing related studies at https://github.com/QinzheYang/Awesome-RS-State-Space-Model .

title: Mamba-based mutual reinforce diffusion model for unaligned hyperspectral-RGB multimodal change detection
abstract: Hyperspectral image (HSI) has become an important source of data for analyzing subtle surface changes; however, most existing HSI change detection (CD) methods are restricted to precisely aligned multitemporal homogeneous HSIs, which are difficult to obtain in real scenes. To overcome this limitation, HSI-RGB multimodal CD incorporates RGB images, enabling collaborative detection across different satellite platforms. Although this approach has been shown to have high potential, challenges such as modality differences and spatial deformation limit the direct application of existing HSI-CD methods. This study proposes a Mamba-based mutual reinforce diffusion model for unaligned HSI-RGB multimodal CD, achieving mutual reinforcement between image registration and CD through a conditional diffusion mechanism, thereby effectively identifying changes in terms of spatial deformation and modality difference. Specifically, a spatial-modal alignment diffusion network is designed to implement bidirectional super-resolution and registration, alleviating modality differences and spatial misalignment and enabling the accurate extraction of changed information. By applying a change-aware matching strategy, the registration block utilizes feedback from change maps to correct misalignment. Subsequently, a spectral-spatial-temporal Mamba CD module is proposed, which effectively models spatial, temporal, and spectral correlations of the aligned bitemporal images, achieving accurate CD results. Extensive experiments have demonstrated the superiority of the proposed method relative to existing approaches.

title: RF-based multi-drone detection and classification under open-set setting
abstract: Detecting unauthorized drone intrusions via radio frequency (RF) signals is critical for mitigating severe threats to public safety. However, existing RF-based multi-drone monitoring systems predominantly rely on closed-set assumptions, inevitably misclassifying unknown drone signals as known classes or background noise, thereby failing to secure airspace against novel intruders. To address this issue, we propose a novel coarse-to-fine framework designed specifically for open-set multi-drone flight control signal (FCS) detection and classification. First, by exploiting the intrinsic morphological characteristics of FCS hopping bursts in the time-frequency domain, we design a class-agnostic proposal generation module to capture all potential signal bursts in the spectrogram, ensuring high recall for both known and unknown FCSs. Second, we construct semantics for each FCS hopping burst by fusing the texture feature, the geometry feature and the position feature. These features are refined via deformable attention modules to extract precise FCS details, followed by a global self-attention mechanism explicitly modeling the intra-frame correlations among disjoint FCS bursts. Third, we leverage a multi-objective optimization strategy to regularize the global semantic distribution and enforce intra-frame semantic consistency. Building upon this semantic distribution, the framework adaptively rejects unknown FCSs through outlier analysis and subsequently refines their categories via clustering. Extensive experiments on real-world datasets demonstrate that the proposed method significantly outperforms existing methods in terms of detection accuracy and open-set generalizability, effectively classifying both known and unknown drones.

title: Robust radar-optical fusion for low-altitude target recognition under time-varying heterogeneous degradation
abstract: Reliable recognition of low-altitude targets, such as unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) and birds, is important for low-altitude airspace security. Radar-optical fusion provides complementary micro-motion and appearance cues for target recognition but is challenged by time-varying heterogeneous degradation: the two modalities undergo distinct degradations whose severities vary dynamically with weak cross-modal correlation. Specifically, fog and low illumination weaken texture and contour information in optical images, whereas clutter interference obscures micro-Doppler structures in radar spectrograms. Consequently, the reliability of the two modalities fluctuates independently over time, deteriorating multimodal fusion performance. To address this challenge, this paper proposes a radar-optical robust fusion network (RORF Net). The framework integrates three key components. First, a gradient-aware and semantically guided enhancement network extracts degradation-robust structural representations by modeling optical texture and contour patterns together with radar micro-Doppler ridges. Second, a confidence-driven dynamic gating module estimates sample-level modality reliability and adaptively regulates the contribution of each modality through bidirectional cross-modal interaction. Third, a cross-modal semantic alignment module maps radar and optical representations into a common semantic space through supervised contrastive learning. The network is optimized using a two-stage training strategy that first establishes cross-modal alignment and then enforces global semantic refinement. Experiments on our radar-optical multimodal dataset demonstrate that RORF Net attains an overall accuracy of 96.45%, surpassing existing state-of-the-art multimodal fusion algorithms by 8.71%. Ablation studies confirm its effectiveness under time-varying heterogeneous degradation.

title: Exploring dispersion of feature distribution from parameters for network pruning
abstract: Network pruning achieves significant advancements in deploying models on devices with constrained computational resources. Existing filter pruning methods adopt the criterion that features contributing less to the output are less important. However, they overlook the capability of features to capture crucial distinctions between various samples faithfully. In this paper, we employ the dispersion of feature distribution as an indicator of this capability and propose to preserve channels with large dispersion. The proposed distribution-based dispersion filter pruning method (DDisp) estimates the variance and coefficient of variation (CV) of each channel’s feature distribution. To measure the dispersion, we exploit the approximated probability density of the distribution and establish mathematically grounded estimations towards the real variance and CV. Moreover, these estimations are built upon the stored parameters of normalization layers. This enables DDisp to circumvent the additional overhead inherent to data-driven methods, namely the costly network inference phase and the aggregation of actual statistics from a multitude of features. Extensive experiments demonstrate that DDisp consistently achieves excellent performance on various architectures, including ResNet, MobileNet, DenseNet, VGG, and ViT.

title: Automatic TCAD calibration based on Bayesian optimization for SiC MOSFET
Learning from the unseen: generative data augmentation for geometric-semantic accident anticipation
abstract: Anticipating traffic accidents is a critical yet unresolved problem for autonomous driving, hindered by the inherent complexity of modeling interactions between road users and the limited availability of diverse, large-scale datasets. To address these issues, we propose a dual-path framework. On the one hand, we employ a video synthesis pipeline that, guided by structured prompts, derives feature distributions from existing corpora and produces high-fidelity synthetic driving scenes consistent with the statistical patterns of real data. On the other hand, we design a graph neural network enriched with semantic cues, enabling dynamic reasoning over both spatial and semantic relations among participants. To validate the effectiveness of our approach, we release a new benchmark dataset containing standardized, finely annotated video sequences that cover a broad spectrum of regions, weather, and traffic conditions. Evaluations across existing datasets and our new benchmark confirm notable gains in both accuracy and anticipation lead time, highlighting the capacity of the proposed framework to mitigate current data bottlenecks and enhance the reliability of autonomous driving systems.

title: Quantization-aware Bayesian inference framework for unsourced random access in backhaul-limited cell-free massive MIMO systems
abstract: In this paper, we consider joint active user detection, channel estimation and data decoding for unsourced random access (URA) in cell-free massive multiple-input multiple-output (CF-mMIMO) systems with backhaul constraints, where the access points (APs) may receive concurrent transmissions from hundreds of low-power terminal devices. In such scenarios, the coarse quantization of baseband signals at APs introduces nonlinear distortion that severely degrades joint detection and decoding. To address this issue, we develop a Bayesian inference framework that models the quantized observations as a generalized linear model (GLM). By building upon this model, we extend the vector approximate message passing net (VAMP-Net) and MIMO low-density parity-check net (MIMO-LDPC-Net) into generalized VAMP-Net and generalized MIMO-LDPC-Net, enabling quantization-aware joint activity detection, channel estimation, and data decoding. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed approach achieves at least an order of magnitude lower detection and decoding error rates than the existing linear-model-based algorithms, particularly under low-bit backhaul quantization, while maintaining moderate additional computational overhead compared with SLM-based unfolded receivers, making it suitable for large-scale CF-mMIMO systems.

title: Decentralized direct localization of low-altitude targets in clock-asynchronous multi-sensor networks
abstract: Accurate multi-station positioning is a key enabler for low-altitude economy applications such as unmanned aerial vehicle monitoring, aerial logistics, and safety supervision. However, low-altitude sensing networks are often bandwidth-constrained, dynamically deployed, and difficult to synchronize, which makes conventional centralized direct localization unattractive. This paper develops a lightweight decentralized direct localization framework for clock-asynchronous multi-sensor networks (MSNs). The method consists of a local-estimation stage and a fusion-update stage. In the local stage, each node refines a coarse state estimate based on its local likelihood while jointly accounting for the node-specific clock offset, where a trust-region-enhanced Gauss-Newton solver is employed to achieve efficient iterative refinement without exhaustive grid search. In the fusion stage, neighboring nodes exchange only low-dimensional intermediate messages, and a Fisher-information-guided weighted consensus together with node scheduling is used to improve global positioning accuracy and scalability. The proposed framework preserves the accuracy advantage of direct localization while substantially reducing communication overhead and removing the need for a centralized fusion center. Numerical results show that the proposed scheme achieves performance close to centralized direct localization and outperforms representative decentralized baselines under asynchronous conditions.

title: Optimal sparse conformal array design for dual-polarized weather radar with integrated communications in low-altitude airspace
abstract: The safety and efficiency of the low-altitude economy (LAE) are highly dependent on high-fidelity, real-time awareness of micro-scale meteorological conditions. Hazardous low-altitude weather phenomena, such as localized wind shear and intense precipitation, pose significant risks to unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) operations. This paper investigates an airship-borne dual-polarized weather radar system with integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) capabilities, designed to provide persistent, high-resolution monitoring of the low-altitude atmospheric environment. To reconcile the requirements for large-aperture sensing with the aerodynamic and payload constraints of low-altitude platforms, we propose a joint design of a sparse conformal array and beamforming. A dual-polarized conformal detection model is established to extract high-resolution polarimetric signatures, which are essential for detecting hazardous weather in complex low-altitude terrains. Leveraging this model, a polarized transmit beampattern modulation scheme is developed to embed critical flight-safety data into polarization components, enabling a threefold increase in data rate for air-to-ground and air-to-air coordination. The joint optimization of the sparse array configuration and beamformer is formulated as a multivariate combinatorial problem and solved using the alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM). This ensures robust performance across diverse scanning angles required for wide-area low-altitude surveillance. Simulation results, including multi-channel meteorological echoes based on WSR-88D data, demonstrate that the proposed system achieves superior performance in both sensing accuracy and communication throughput, offering a viable solution for the integrated sensing and communication infrastructure essential to the low-altitude economy.

title: Delay-energy tradeoff for cooperative ISAC systems: a learning-based multi-objective optimization approach
abstract: This paper investigates cooperative integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) systems, where multiple base stations (BSs) equipped with edge servers perform target detection for aerial and ground targets. To support cooperative sensing services, sensing data for the same target are collected by multiple spatially distributed BSs. The data are then aggregated at a designated BS and processed using its computing resources. Given the model, a multi-objective optimization problem is formulated to balance task delay and energy consumption under constraints on available resources and cooperative detection probability. The problem is then transformed into a multi-objective Markov decision process (MOMDP) to maximize the expected cumulative reward. Next, a learning-based algorithm is employed to solve the MOMDP, in which an evolutionary multi-objective (EMO) framework is combined with a hybrid proximal policy optimization (PPO) algorithm enhanced by a space-time self-attention (STSA) module. To maintain diversity and prevent premature convergence, a fitness-sharing strategy is applied during population updates to enable the identification of well-distributed Pareto-optimal policies. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed EMO-STSA-PPO framework achieves faster convergence and better Pareto solution quality than benchmark schemes, and provides a superior energy-delay tradeoff under the same resource constraints. Moreover, the effects of bandwidth and computation resources on the delay-energy tradeoff are analyzed, as well as the overall system performance under detection probability constraints.

Mutually reinforcing effect between ferroelectric polarization and charge trapping in FeFET-based NAND flash memory
abstract: To assist with the future application of ferroelectric materials in 3D NAND flash memory, we clarify the coupling mechanism between ferroelectric polarization and charge trapping, which intensifies the memory window (MW), in a gate-stack ferroelectric field-effect transistor (FeFET). Based on Gauss’s law, the mutual reinforcement effect is revealed: the charge trapping efficiency is boosted as a result of ultrafast polarization switching, and the trapped charge, in turn, improves remanent polarization. The MW is consistently enlarged through the coupling mechanism for an FeFET with dominant gate-side injection, while it depends on the competition between charge trapping enhancement and the MW counteracting effect for an FeFET with dominant channel-side injection. Through an in-depth investigation of the quantitative relationships between the MW and FeFET parameters, we explain the intrinsic mechanism of the MW enlargement/narrowing phenomenon using crucial theoretical formulas. With engineering optimization, such a coupling mechanism can intensify the MW in an FeFET by more than 50%. These findings will benefit further studies on hafnium-based nonvolatile memory.

Integrated sensing, communications, and identification for low-altitude economy
abstract: Abstract With the rapid development of the low-altitude economy (LAE), low-altitude activities are becoming increasingly frequent and dynamic, placing growing demands on the underlying information infrastructure to ensure efficient and safe airspace operation. Low-altitude information networks (LAINs), as the key infrastructure supporting these activities, are required not only to ensure reliable communication, but also to support environmental sensing and target identification. Existing research on integrated sensing and communications (ISAC) has established an important foundation for the joint design of communication and sensing functions in LAINs. However, with the increasing need for airspace safety and regulatory compliance, identification is becoming an essential function that should be systematically incorporated into the overall network design. This paper presents a comprehensive review of integrated sensing, communications, and identification (ISCAI) for LAE. We first provide an overview of LAINs by reviewing approaches to low-altitude communication, sensing, and identification, and explain how representative application scenarios motivate their integration. We then review the fundamentals of low-altitude ISAC, including system architectures, channel modeling, unified signal models, and performance metrics, followed by communication-centric and sensing-centric ISAC design as well as resource allocation and aircraft trajectory optimization. Building on these, we introduce the ISCAI paradigm, with particular attention to a backscatter communication (BackCom)-based identification mechanism in which backscatter devices serve as electronic license plates for aircraft. We further present the system and signal models of the resulting integrated sensing and identification (ISAI) and ISCAI paradigms, along with their multifunctional receiver designs and mutual integration gains. Finally, we outline important open problems and future directions, including the information-theoretic framework of ISCAI, artificial intelligence (AI)-empowered ISCAI system design, and reconfigurable intelligent surface-enhanced ISCAI. This paper aims to provide a structured perspective on how LAINs are evolving from the joint design of communication and sensing toward a broader integration of communication, sensing, and identification.
